title: Control Systems
tagline: Modelling dynamic systems, transfer functions, time response, stability, root locus, frequency response, PID, state-space and digital control
summary: Feedback control keeps aircraft stable, robots on their paths and engines at speed. The course models mechanical, electrical, fluid and thermal systems with differential equations and transfer functions, analyses transient and steady-state response and stability, and designs controllers by root locus, frequency response and state-space methods, with PID control and digital implementation.

chapters.title: Modelling dynamic systems
chapters.summary: Differential equations of mechanical, electrical, fluid and thermal systems, linearisation and analogies between domains.

chapters.title: Transfer functions and block diagrams
chapters.summary: The Laplace transform, transfer functions, poles and zeros, and block-diagram algebra.

chapters.title: Time response
chapters.summary: First- and second-order responses, rise time, overshoot and settling time, and the effect of additional poles and zeros.

chapters.title: Feedback and stability
chapters.summary: The benefits of feedback, steady-state error and system type, and stability by the Routh–Hurwitz criterion.

chapters.title: Root-locus design
chapters.summary: Sketching the root locus, and designing gains and lead and lag compensators with it.

chapters.title: Frequency response
chapters.summary: Bode plots, the Nyquist criterion, gain and phase margins, and loop shaping.

chapters.title: PID control
chapters.summary: Proportional, integral and derivative action, tuning rules, integrator wind-up and practical implementation.

chapters.title: State-space methods
chapters.summary: State equations, controllability and observability, pole placement and state observers.

chapters.title: Digital control
chapters.summary: Sampling, the z-transform, discrete equivalents of continuous controllers, and implementation on microcontrollers.
